steps.title: Prepare 10× PBS stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve NaCl (80 g, 1.37 M), KCl (2 g, 27 mM), NaH₂PO₄ (14.4 g, 100 mM) and KH₂PO₄ (2.4 g, 18 mM) in distilled water and bring the volume to 1 L; adjust pH to 7.4, store at 25 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS working solution
steps.instruction: Mix 50 mL of the 10× PBS stock with 450 mL of double‑distilled water (ddH₂O) to obtain 500 mL of 1× PBS; store at 25 °C for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Prepare PBST solution
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of Tween‑20 to 50 mL of 1× PBS to obtain a 0.1 % (v/v) PBST solution; use ddH₂O for dilution.

steps.title: Prepare 7% blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.7 g of BSA or skimmed milk powder in 10 mL of PBST to obtain a 7 % (w/v) blocking buffer; prepare fresh when required.

steps.title: Prepare 2% blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.2 g of BSA or skimmed milk powder in 10 mL of PBST to obtain a 2 % (w/v) blocking buffer; prepare fresh when required (used for antibody dilutions).

steps.title: Prepare 70% ethanol
steps.instruction: Mix 350 mL absolute ethanol with 50 mL water to obtain 400 mL of 70 % ethanol; prepare fresh when required.

steps.title: Prepare 10× transfer buffer stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve Tris (30.2 g, 25 mM) and Glycine (144 g, 192 mM) in water and bring the volume to 1 L; store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare 1× transfer buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute 100 mL of the 10× transfer buffer stock with 200 mL methanol, then bring the final volume to 1 L with water; store at 4 °C and reuse for two weeks.

steps.title: Prepare stripping buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve Glycine (1.5 g, 199 mM), SDS (0.1 g, 0.1 % w/v) and Tween‑20 (1 mL, 1 % v/v) in water and bring the volume to 100 mL; adjust pH to 2.2; keep at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Ponceau S staining solution
steps.instruction: Make 50 mL of fresh 0.1 % (w/v) Ponceau S solution in water; store at room temperature for short‑term use.

steps.title: Thaw and seed HEK293 cells
steps.instruction: Retrieve a 2.0 mL cryovial of HEK293 cells from –80 °C or liquid nitrogen (use cryogenic gloves), thaw in a 37 °C water bath for 2–3 min, add 1 mL serum‑free DMEM, transfer to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 800 × g for 3 min. Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL fresh complete DMEM (10 % heat‑inactivated FBS, 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin), count ~8 × 10⁵ cells and seed them into a T‑25 flask. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified incubator for 12–16 h. The next day replace medium with 3 mL fresh complete DMEM.

steps.title: Split, count, and reseed cells
steps.instruction: Discard medium from the confluent T‑25 flask, add 1 mL 1× Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 3 min at 37 °C, observe detachment, then add 1 mL complete DMEM to neutralize trypsin and collect cells into a fresh 15 mL Falcon tube (optional: add 1 mL serum‑free DMEM to recover leftover cells). Centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min, wash pellet with 1 mL serum‑free DMEM (or 500 µL DMEM + 500 µL 1× PBS), resuspend, centrifuge again at 500 × g for 3 min, discard supernatant, add 1 mL fresh complete DMEM and gently resuspend. Prepare two or three new T‑25 flasks with 3 mL complete DMEM each and add 200 µL of the resuspended cell suspension (dilution 1:10 or 1:15). Gently rock flasks and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Count viable cells with trypan blue
steps.instruction: Take 1 mL of the cell suspension, mix 100 µL trypan blue with 100 µL cell suspension in a 1.5 mL tube, gently pipette, load 10 µL under the hemocytometer coverslip, and count viable cells in the four large squares. Calculate cells / mL using (cells in 4 squares / 4) × 10⁴ × dilution factor (dilution factor = 2). Example: 1000 cells → 5 × 10⁶ cells/mL. To obtain 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, mix 200 µL cell suspension with 800 µL complete DMEM. Seed 1 × 10⁶ cells per 60 mm dish and incubate 12–14 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until ~80 % confluency.

steps.title: Prepare plasmid DNA mixes (Mix‑1)
steps.instruction: In 0.5 mL tubes keep 20–30 µL aliquots of each plasmid (pcDNA3.1‑c‑myc, pEGFP‑N1, pcDNA3.1‑c‑myc‑EDRF1, pEGFP‑N1‑NS2BNS3pro) at –20 °C. For each transfection condition add the indicated plasmids (e.g., 1 µg pcDNA3.1‑c‑myc + 1 µg pEGFP‑N1) into OptiMEM (Mix‑1) and incubate 2–3 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Lipofectamine mixes (Mix‑2)
steps.instruction: In separate 1.5 mL tubes add Lipofectamine 2000 to OptiMEM: 2 µL for single‑plasmid transfections, 4 µL for co‑transfections (plasmid total 2 µg). Incubate 2–3 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Form DNA‑Lipofectamine complexes
steps.instruction: Combine Mix‑1 with Mix‑2, gently mix, and incubate 20 min at room temperature to allow complex formation.

steps.title: Transfect cells and post‑transfection incubation
steps.instruction: Add the DNA‑Lipofectamine complex dropwise onto the 60 mm dishes (previously ~80 % confluent) and incubate 5–6 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Replace the medium with fresh complete DMEM and culture for an additional 48 h.

steps.title: Harvest cells and prepare whole‑cell lysate
steps.instruction: After 48 h, aspirate medium, add 1 mL 1× PBS, scrape cells with a cell scraper, collect into a 1.5 mL tube and centrifuge 800 × g for 5 min. Wash pellet twice with 1 mL 1× PBS (centrifuge 800 × g, 5 min each). Resuspend pellet in 200 µL RIPA buffer plus 20 µL 1× protease inhibitor cocktail, vortex three times with 5‑min intervals, keep on ice 30 min. Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 15 min, transfer supernatant (whole‑cell lysate) to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Quantify protein and run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration using Bradford reagent, load 60 µg of each lysate onto a 10 % SDS‑PAGE gel and perform electrophoresis.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to PVDF membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer the resolved proteins onto a PVDF membrane in 1× transfer buffer at 80 V for 3 h (or 50 V overnight) using a wet‑transfer unit.

steps.title: Stain membrane with Ponceau S
steps.instruction: Immerse the membrane in 4–5 mL fresh Ponceau S solution for 5 min with gentle rocking, then remove stain, collect it for reuse (up to twice), wash briefly with ddH₂O, image the stained bands, and wash the membrane with 1× PBST until the stain is completely removed.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in 7 % blocking buffer for 2 h at room temperature with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Rinse membrane once with 1× PBST, then add anti‑Myc Tag primary antibody (1.4 µg/mL, 1:1000) diluted in either 1× PBST or 2 % blocking buffer. Incubate 2 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C with gentle rocking.

steps.title: Wash membrane after primary
steps.instruction: Wash 1× PBST three times, 10 min each, on a rocker with mild agitation.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Add anti‑mouse IgG HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody (1:10,000) diluted in 1× PBST, incubate 2 h at room temperature with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Wash membrane after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash 1× PBST three times, 15 min each, on a rocker with high agitation.

steps.title: Develop blot
steps.instruction: Apply Femto LUCENT™ PLUS‑HRP substrate to the membrane and capture the chemiluminescent image using a Bio‑Rad ChemiDoc imaging system.

steps.title: Strip membrane
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with ddH₂O twice for 5 min each (medium agitation), then wash 1× PBST twice for 5 min each. Add ~10 mL stripping buffer, incubate 30 min at room temperature with medium agitation. Discard stripping buffer, wash ddH₂O 5 min, wash 1× PBS twice for 5 min each, and finally wash 1× PBST twice for 10 min each. The membrane is now ready for re‑probing.

steps.title: Re‑probe with new antibodies
steps.instruction: Block the stripped membrane again with 7 % blocking buffer for 2 h at room temperature, then incubate with anti‑GFP primary antibody (1:1000) followed by anti‑rabbit HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody (0.04 µg/mL, 1:10,000) using the same incubation and wash conditions as described above, and develop as before.
